problem: VLN agents (including VLN-CE and physical-robot ones) are trained with one fixed camera configuration (1.5 m height, 90° HFOV), so navigation skills fail to transfer to robots with different camera height or HFOV. Retraining the whole policy for each robot needs a lot of data and cost.
motivation: Real robots (sweepers, drones, quadrupeds) have very different camera heights and fields of view, creating a large gap in visual input. Since the camera only changes the image observations, the authors argue the problem lies in the visual perception module and can be fixed there while the language and navigation-reasoning modules are frozen.
key_idea: Freeze the language and navigation modules and meta-learn only the ResNet50 visual perception module (via MAML few-shot adaptation or via learning-to-learn feature-wise affine transformation layers) so that features under a new camera match those of the original camera at the same location.
insight: Baseline navigation collapses under camera change (e.g. CMA SR 0.32 to 0.04 at 0.2 m height), confirming the perception gap, and aligning only the visual features recovers much of it (CMA+MAML SR 0.23 and CMA+AT 0.24 on val-unseen). MAML is slightly better in seen environments, while AT layers are slightly better in unseen ones and need no adaptation data; the authors attribute this to MAML adaptation being biased by the seen/unseen gap. The differences between the two are small, though.
method: Modular split: VLN model divided into visual perception (two ResNet50s for RGB and depth), language understanding, and navigation reasoning; only the perception module is adapted, and the action space is assumed identical across agents.

Feature-distillation objective: the original trained ResNets serve as teachers; the new ResNets are trained with an L1 loss so that features from the new camera at the same state match the original camera's features (L_r for RGB, L_d for depth).

MAML few-shot adaptation: tasks are support sets of k=3 RGB/depth images from cameras with different configurations; inner-loop gradient steps (10 steps, inner and outer lr 2e-4, Adam) adapt the ResNets, and an outer update optimizes the initialization.

Learning-to-learn affine transformation (AT): feature-wise AT layers are inserted in the ResNets, with scale and bias sampled from Gaussians whose std parameters are learned; ResNet weights are updated on a pseudo-seen camera domain, AT parameters are updated by the loss on a pseudo-unseen domain with AT removed; no adaptation is needed at test time.
Navigation baselines: Seq2Seq (GRU) and Cross-Modal Attention (two GRUs with attention) from VLN-CE, using pre-trained checkpoints (DAgger; CMA with progress monitor and augmentation).

setting.backbone: ResNet50 (RGB and depth) visual perception module meta-trained; frozen Seq2Seq / CMA VLN-CE policies (GRU/LSTM)
setting.training_data: VLN-CE pretrained baselines; perception module meta-trained on observations from 3 camera configs (heights 0.5/1.0/1.5 m at 90° HFOV, or HFOVs 90/120/150° at 1.5 m); MAML uses 3-shot support sets
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth with varied camera height/HFOV, plus instruction
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 15°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (MAML uses a few target-camera samples for adaptation; AT uses none)

numbers.extra: trained on 0.5/1.0/1.5 m cameras at 90° HFOV, tested at 0.2 m with no adaptation
3-shot adaptation on the target camera, 10 gradient steps
trained on 90/120/150° HFOV at 1.5 m, tested at 60° with no adaptation

numbers_note: Metrics printed as fractions (0-1) in the paper, kept as printed. Only selected variants listed; Seq2seq+MAML and HFOV Seq2seq rows also exist in Table 3. Val-seen HFOV rows not listed.
results: Changing camera height to 0.2 m or HFOV to 60° drops baselines sharply (e.g. CMA SR 0.32 to 0.04 at 0.2 m). Both meta-learning methods recover much of this (CMA val-unseen SR 0.23 MAML / 0.24 AT vs 0.04 baseline), still below the original-camera SR of 0.32; MAML is better in seen environments, AT slightly better in unseen.
limitations: Only camera height and HFOV tested on a single test configuration each (0.2 m, 60°); performance remains well below the original-camera performance.
Differences between MAML and AT are small (about 0.01-0.02 SR) with no significance analysis; explanation is speculative.
Simulation-only evaluation, no real robots; assumes identical action space across robots.
builds_on: Few-shot adaptation of visual navigation (Luo et al.)
